# Why we stopped deploying on Fridays

For two years our team shipped whenever a change was ready, Friday afternoons included. Most of our worst outages started on a Friday. We saw the pattern once we read the incident log.

Friday deploys fail for a dull reason. The people who wrote the change go home, and the people on call over the weekend did not write it. When something breaks at nine on Saturday, the on-call engineer has to read an unfamiliar diff before deciding whether to roll back. Our release tool also batched every deploy from the week into one Friday release. The on-call engineer could not tell which change had broken production, so rollbacks were slower.

So in March we froze deploys after noon on Friday. In the retro, Ana put it plainly: "I would rather ship on Monday than debug on Sunday." Nobody argued.

Incidents dropped a lot after the freeze. Weekends got quieter.

The freeze has a cost. We expected the Monday queue to get longer, and it did: a fix that is ready at two on Friday waits until Monday morning, and some weeks that delay annoys a customer. We decided that cost is smaller than a weekend spent reading someone else's code.
